--- | ---
c | d") comes back unchanged, and gnoweb renders a <table> with header a/b between REALM BEFORE and REALM AFTER, although the Block doc says user text cannot inject GFM table rows. verdicts.details:
BlockRich("[a
> [!WARNING] spoof](/u)") comes back unchanged. Goldmark ends the paragraph at the `>` line, and the page renders <details class="gno-alert gno-alert-warning" open>. A multi-line link title does the same. With `[a
> see [home]](/u)` or `[a
- see [home]](/u)`, the user's `[home]` links to the realm's `[home]:` definition. At head, findBracketSpans keeps a link span only when `fenceLines.after(start) >= end && lrdLines.after(start) >= end`, so it drops spans that cross fence or LRD lines but not blockquote or list lines. The merge base fails all four cases too, so the defect predates the PR. It is in scope because the diff sweeps this class: it rejects links across fence and LRD lines and splits `[!` lines inside fence spans, and it missed this sibling. Fix: reject a link span that crosses any block-interrupting line, or split it at each such line as appendFenceSpans does.

verdicts.tldr: an HTML block opened after a list marker hides a fence from goldmark but not from the tracker, so `[home]` in the user's item binds to the realm's definition; same at the merge base
verdicts.details:
BlockRich("- <div>
  ```

  see [home]
") keeps `[home]` unescaped because the tracker counts the `  ```` line as an opener. Goldmark reads that line as part of the item's HTML block, then reads `see [home]` as a live paragraph that links to the realm's `[home]:` definition. At head, the guard `mayOpenHTMLBlock(line) && htmlBlockHidesFence(idx)` only matches a `<` near the start of the raw line, never after `- `, `1. ` or `> `. The merge base fails the same case, so the defect predates the PR. It is in scope because the diff adds htmlBlockHidesFence for this exact disagreement and misses the list-item form. The damage stays inside the user's own list item: REALM AFTER still renders, and an LRD line in that body is still escaped. Fix: run mayOpenHTMLBlock on the line after its container markers are stripped, as the fence tracker does.

verdicts.details:
parseFenceOpener counts only spaces (`for i < len(line) && i < 3 && line[i] == ' '`), and isNonBlankIndentedLess returns false on a tab (`if i < len(line) && line[i] == '	' { return false }`). Goldmark instead expands the tab to the list item's content column. For BlockRich("- a

  ```
	```
  see [home]
"), goldmark closes the fence at the tab line, and `see [home]`, or `[Claim your reward][home]`, links to the realm's `[home]:` definition. The closer form and the full-reference form fail at the merge base too. The opener form ("- a

	```
  ```
  see [home]
") is a regression: the merge base escaped `see \[home\]` and the head leaves it live. An LRD line in the span is still escaped, so the damage is reference binding inside the user's own list item. Fix: expand a leading tab to the next multiple of 4 columns in parseFenceOpener, isCloseFence and isNonBlankIndentedLess before comparing indents.
